title: The Paradise PVGA1A's extended registers
covers: The Paradise PVGA1A's Paradise registers, reached through the graphics index port 03CE and the data port 03CF, as the maker's datasheet documents them, and what DOSBox-X does with each.

rows.text: The graphics controller index register is read/write at port 03CE.
Bits 7-4 of the index register are reserved, and bits 3-0 point at one graphics controller register.
All the Paradise registers reside at index pointers beyond the graphics controller registers.
The PVGA1A adds six lock-protected I/O registers in the graphics controller section, at register locations IBM did not use; all are readable and writable.
DOSBox-X registers write_p3ce at port 0x3ce, and read_p3ce there on VGA machines.
An index above eight is handed to the installed SVGA handler as the register number; the Paradise handler is installed at setup.
The other graphics register is read/write at port 03CF.
A register is written XXX.YY, XXX the data port and YY the index (the capture prints OF for 0F): write 0F to 3CE, then the data byte to 3CF.
The register table names the registers PR0A and PR0B, which the capture prints PROA and PROB, PR1 to PR5, and the configuration field CNF.
The I/O location of each register is 3CF with its index 09 to 0F, the capture printing some zeroes as letter O.
DOSBox-X registers write_p3cf at port 0x3cf, and read_p3cf there on VGA machines.
SVGA_Setup_ParadisePVGA1A hangs write_p3cf_pvga1a and read_p3cf_pvga1a on the two dispatch pointers the 3CF handlers call.
For an index above eight the 3CF handlers pass the stored index and the byte to the Paradise write and read functions.
An index the Paradise handler has no case for is logged as illegal and changes nothing.
A read of an index the handler has no case for is logged as illegal and returns zero.
PRO A is the address offset register A, read and written at port 3CF with index 09.
The registers hold an offset added to the system address when accessing 1MB of video memory; register A is primary, always enabled; B only if PR1 bit 3 is 1.
PROA is always enabled when PR1 bit 3 is 0.
PROA is normally used to control 64KB of the video address space.
The six-bit offset is added to address bits 12-18 of the system address bus to form a 20-bit address, in 4KB segments.
The register holds reserved and offset bits, added to the system address and selected when address bit A15 is 1; register A is the default.
The video memory space starts at A0000H (the capture prints O for 0) and ends at BFFFFH, limited to a 64KB partition so a second video card can co-exist.
Register A drives the bank when PR1 bit 3 is 0; with bit 3 set the dual-bank branch stores nothing, so register B never drives the window.
The setup tests PR1 bit 3 only and makes PR0A the bank of the whole window; address bit A15 selects nothing.
The window size and its granularity come from the configuration; the Paradise default is a 64KB window with 4KB granularity.
The bank is taken from all eight bits of PR0A, where the document gives a six-bit offset; the window keeps the document's 4KB granularity by default.
PRO B is written at port 3CF with index 0A, which the capture prints as OA, and read back there.
PROA and PROB may access two 32KB windows, PROA from A8000H-AFFFFH and PROB from A0000H when PR1 bit 3 is set; the capture garbles PROB's end.
The alternate offset bits are selected by the system address only if PR1 bit 3 is 1.
A write stores PR0B, but the dual-bank branch is empty, so the bank still comes from register A.
The branch PR1 bit 3 would take is empty, so no offset from register B ever reaches the video memory window.
PR1 is the eight-bit memory size register, read and written at port 3CF with index 0B, which the capture prints as OB.
All PR registers except PR1 bits 1-0 are 0 at power on reset; PR1 bits 1-0 latch from the memory data bus pins, and a pullup latches them low.
256KB of video memory is four 64KB maps defining bit planes 0-3, chained into one large plane in mode 13.
The start of the video buffer is configurable (the capture prints O for 0): 64KB or 128KB segments can start at A0000H, and 32KB segments at B0000H or B8000H.
Bits 6 and 7 extend the video buffer to 512KB or 1024KB.
The memory size field selects one of four memory sizes: 256KB VGA, 256 PVGA, 512 PVGA or 1024 PVGA.
A field maps the BIOS ROM out when set to 1.
A field gives the BIOS ROM a 16-bit data path, and 0 selects an eight-bit path.
A field enables a 16-bit wide bus for video memory.
A field enables alternate address offset register B, and 0 enables the primary register A.
The memory map field selects VGA mapping, the first 256KB or 512KB in 1MB space, or 1024KB in a larger space.
The emulator starts PR1 at zero and sets its memory size field from the configured video memory; no data bus pin is latched.
The buffer's start is not taken from PR1: the memory size alone is configured, and the window comes from the VBE settings.
A write stores bit 3 only and keeps every other bit, so the BIOS ROM mapping field cannot be changed.
A write stores bit 3 only, so the BIOS ROM data path width field is never written.
A write stores bit 3 only, so the field that enables a 16-bit video memory bus keeps its value.
Bit 3 is stored and tested, but the dual-bank branch is empty, so the field never enables register B.
A write stores bit 3 only, so no value of the memory map field reaches the emulator.
The setup installs the two handlers and caps the SVGA width at 2048 and the height at 1024.
The setup hangs the mode-set, determine, clock and accepts functions on the driver, and calls VGA_SetClock with CLK_25, CLK_28, 32400 and 35900.
The memory defaults to 512KB, and PR1's size field is set to 1, 2 or 3 for 256KB, 512KB or 1024KB.
The setup's last act is a write of 05H to port 0x3cf.
The setup writes the size field from the configured memory as 1, 2 or 3; the 256KB VGA value 0 is never programmed.
A write stores bit 3 only, so a program cannot set bits 6 and 7; the setup sets them from the configured memory size.
PR2 is written at port 3CF with index 0C, which the capture prints as OC, and read back there.
A bit selects 6845 compatibility mode, VGA mode when 0, and enables M24 mode.
A character map select bit, with PR2(2) and attribute bit 4, selects character maps from planes 2 or 3.
A character clock period field selects the IBM VGA 8 or 9 dot clock, 7 dots for 132-character mode, 9 dots or 10 dots.
A bit enables a special color underline on odd numbered attributes and, with PR2(5), the character map selection.
A bit is the third clock select line to an external clock chip when CNF(3) is 1; otherwise the internal clock multiplexor is locked.
A bit sets the horizontal sync timing for 8 or 9 dots per character, and 16 or 18 dots when 0.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: no mode is selected from the register.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: no character map is selected from the register.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: the character clock is not changed by the register.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: no underline mode and no character map is enabled.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: no clock select line is driven.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: the horizontal sync timing is not changed.
PR3 is written at port 3CF with index 0D, which the capture prints as OD, and read back there.
The document writes a CRT controller register bit as 3?5.11(7), meaning bit 7 of data register 11 written through index 3?4.
Register locking is controlled by PR3 bits 5, 1 and 0 and by CRT controller register 11 bit 7.
Group 0, CRT controller registers 00 to 05, is locked when PR3 bit 5 is 1 or register 11 bit 7 is 1.
Group 1, register 07 bits 6 and 1, is locked when PR3 bit 1 is 0 and register 11 bit 7 is 1.
Group 2, register 06 and parts of register 07, is locked when PR3 bit 0 is 1 or register 11 bit 7 is 1.
Group 3, register 09 bit 5, registers 10, 11 bits 3-0, 15 and 16, is locked when PR3 bit 0 is 1.
Group 4, CRT controller mode register 17 bit 2, is locked when PR3 bit 5 is 1.
One bit locks VSYNC polarity as programmed in port 3C2 bit 7.
One bit locks HSYNC polarity as programmed in port 3C2 bit 6.
One bit locks horizontal timing, the registers of groups 0 and 4, and prevents unlocking group 0 by register 11 bit 7.
One bit multiplies the cursor start, stop, preset row scan and maximum scan line values by two.
Two bits are bits 8 and 9 of the CRT start address and the cursor location, character addresses CA(16) and CA(17).
A bit enables the palette registers in non EGA (6845) mode, and in the PVGA1A the palette is enabled all of the time.
A bit prevents applications software from locking the registers of group 1 by setting register 11 bit 7.
A bit maps the BIOS ROM out when set to 1, and a pullup on MD(0) latches it to 0 at power on reset.
Nothing in the write case does it: no CRT controller register is locked from PR3's bits; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: group 0's registers are not locked from PR3; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: group 1's registers are not locked from PR3; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: group 2's registers are not locked from PR3; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: group 3's registers are not locked from PR3; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: CRT controller register 17 is not locked from PR3; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: VSYNC polarity is not locked; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: HSYNC polarity is not locked; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: the horizontal timing registers are not locked; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: the cursor and scan line values are not doubled; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: the palette is not switched by the register; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: nothing prevents a lock of the group 1 registers; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
Nothing in the write case does it: the BIOS ROM is not mapped out from PR3; the body stores the byte and sets the start addresses.
PR4 is written at port 3CF with index 0E, which the capture prints as OE, to tri-state display, video and memory control outputs, and read back there.
Bit 7 controls the BLNKN output: 1 is display enable and 0 is blank.
Bit 6 tri-states the HSYNC, VSYNC and BLNKN output pins.
Bit 5 tri-states the video outputs VID(7:0).
Bit 4 tri-states the memory control outputs.
Bit 3 disables the CGA enable video bit in mode register 3D8.
Bit 2 locks the palette and overscan registers.
Bit 1 is EGA compatible mode: it disables response to I/O 3X8-3XA except 3XA, and the 3C0 and 3C1 registers change to write only.
Bit 0 is the Paradise shift register control, selecting a 256 color mode beyond mode 13's 320 by 200 (the capture gives the resolution as 640(400 by 480)).
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: the BLNKN output is not driven from the register.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: no output pin is tri-stated from the register.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: the video outputs are not tri-stated from the register.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: the memory control outputs are not tri-stated from the register.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: the CGA enable video bit is not disabled from the register.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: the palette and overscan registers are not locked.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: EGA compatible mode is not entered from the register.
Nothing in the write case does it: the handler stores the byte and selects no mode beyond mode 13.
PR5 is the general purpose status and Paradise registers lock/unlock register, read and written at port 3CF with index 0F, which the capture prints as OF.
Bits 7-4 are general purpose read only status bits, latched at power on reset from memory data bus pins MD(7:4); the capture cuts the sentence at the page break.
Bits 2-0 are the Paradise register lock/unlock bits, stored in PR5.
Bit 0 locks vertical timing: it locks the CRTC registers of groups 2 and 3 and overrides an unlock of group 2 by register 11 bit 7.
Registers PR0 through PR4 (the capture prints PRO) are normally locked after power up; PR5 loaded with 05H unlocks them, and any other value locks them again.
A write stores all eight bits, so bits 7-4 are writable rather than the read only status bits the document gives.
The handler stores the byte and nothing else: no CRT controller register is locked by bit 0.
